## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Pilindavacchattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 393) is a canonical verse text belonging to the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the biographical background and meritorious deeds of the elder (*thera*) Pilindavaccha. The SuttaCentral database registers five translations of the text across five modern languages [SuttaCentral].

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus reveals widespread formulaic and narrative text-reuse within the Pali canon and its commentarial literature, recording 448 shared passages across 49 other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial matches occur in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (parts 1 and 2) and the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, reflecting the commentary's integration of the elder's verse narrative [DharmaNexus]. The poem also shares significant verse blocks with numerous other biographical poems in the Therāpadāna, including the *Sucintitattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 430), *Upālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 8), *Bhaddālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 413), *Subhūtittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 23), and *Sāriputtattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 3) [DharmaNexus].

In addition to Pali-internal parallels, DharmaNexus detects cross-linguistic alignments with Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese texts [DharmaNexus]. These include shared passages with Sanskrit narrative works such as the *Mahākarmavibhaṅga*, *Ajitasenavyākaraṇa*, and *Lalitavistara*, as well as Chinese translations of the *Madhyama Āgama* (*Zhong ahan jing*, T 26) and Tibetan translations from the Kangyur and Tengyur, notably the *Vinayavastu* (D0001-2) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
